The five-volume manga states the movie 'was adapted into a five volume manga by Reiji Yamada', with Kankurou Kudou credited for the original story.
Wikipedia states the 2021 animated film is "based on the Japanese manga series of the same name by Jiro Taniguchi"; the manga row credits the same Story & Art author.
Psygnosis's 1997 adventure game is "loosely based on the film of the same name" and casts the player as the film's Miette.
The 2019 Bibury Animation series adapts the 2017 Manjuu/Yongshi mobile game (same Siren/Red Axis war and ship-girl cast).
IGDB: this home-computer port "is based on the first Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles animated series which began airing in late 1987".
Konami's 1989 NES game is a licensed tie-in of the 1987 animated series (Shredder kidnaps April and Splinter); this row is that series' season 6.
The 1989 four-player arcade game is a licensed tie-in of the 1987 animated series ("based on the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles franchise, including the first animated series", Wikipedia).
The 2023 Netflix series is a live-action adaptation of Yoshihiro Togashi’s manga (TMDB keyword “based on manga”).
Wikipedia: the game "shares the same name as the film and is loosely based on the same story" — same demonic-witch premise, not an adaptation of the film.
Both adapt Boris Pasternak's 1957 novel Doctor Zhivago — Lean's 1965 film and ITV's 2002 three-part serial; neither adapts the other.

Both adapt Marvel's Spider-Man comics: Wikipedia calls the 1994 Fox Kids cartoon 'based on the Marvel Comics character of the same name' and the 1977 CBS film is the first live-action Spider-Man production from the same comics. Neither adapts the other; the show-level tie is anchored on this season 4 row, the earliest season in the batch.
The 1977 CBS television film Spider-Man serves as the pilot for The Amazing Spider-Man series, with Nicholas Hammond continuing in the role.
The 1977 CBS television film Spider-Man serves as the pilot for The Amazing Spider-Man series (both seasons), with Nicholas Hammond continuing in the role.

The 76 Oha Suta shorts are a franchise tie-in for Ape Escape, with characters and designs taken from Ape Escape 2 — same continuity as the 1999 game row, but a spin-off rather than a story adaptation.
Saru Getchu: On Air is Xebec's 2006 TV anime based on the Ape Escape games (Wikipedia: "based on the video games"; AniList records the source as a video game); this row is the 1999 first game.
Wikipedia: the Sky/Canal+ series 'is an English-language reimagining of the 1966 Italian film of the same name by Sergio Corbucci', with Schoenaerts in Franco Nero's role — refranchise of the film.
Roar Uthaug's 2018 film is based on the Tomb Raider games and 'primarily inspired by the 2013 video game' — this row.

Both derive from H. G. Wells's 1897 novel: the 2020 film is "loosely based on" it and Wikipedia files the 2000 Sci Fi series under "Television shows based on works by H. G. Wells"; neither adapts the other.
Both adapt Stevenson's 1883 novel: Sky1's 2012 two-part miniseries and Disney's 1950 film are separate adaptations; neither adapts the other.
Both adapt Stevenson's Treasure Island: TMDB tags the 2012 two-part miniseries and the 2007 French L'Île aux Trésors 'based on novel or book'; neither adapts the other.
Both adapt Stevenson's 1883 novel: Sky1's 2012 miniseries and Victor Fleming's 1934 film are separate adaptations; neither adapts the other.

Both adapt Dostoevsky's 1869 novel The Idiot: Kurosawa's 1951 film is 'based on the 1869 novel' and Bortko's 2003 series is 'based on Fyodor Dostoevsky's 1869 novel of the same title'. Neither adapts the other.
The 2010 two-episode OVA adapts Innocent Grey's July 2008 visual novel (Reiji and Toko Kuchiki in 1956), which AniList credits as Original Creator.
MAL describes the webtoon as an "adaptation of the live-action drama series of the same title"; it launched with the SBS series in November 2023.
Both derive from Peyo's Smurfs comics: Infogrames' 1994 platformer (a licensed Franco-Belgian-comics adaptation) and the Hanna-Barbera cartoon, here season 7; neither adapts the other.

Both adapt Robert Louis Stevenson's 1883 novel Treasure Island: Disney's 1950 film states the novel as its source and the 1966 ZDF/ORTF serial is described by its provider as an adaptation of the same novel. Neither adapts the other.
Sankichi Hinodeya's Splatoon manga (one-shot May 2015, then CoroCoro Comic from February 2016) adapts the 2015 Wii U game.
Wikipedia: the BBC series is "a continuation and standalone sequel of the 2021 film Boiling Point", same director/co-writer (Barantini) and much of the cast; TMDB tags the series "based on movie".

Wikipedia: the 2020 film is 'based on the video game series of the same name by Capcom'; this row is the 2004 first entry of that series, so the film adapts the series rather than this title specifically.
Both adapt Mary Shelley's 1818 novel Frankenstein: the 2004 Hallmark miniseries directly and Bernard Rose's 2015 film as 'a modernized adaptation'; neither adapts the other.
MAL's synopsis calls the five-volume Gangan Powered manga 'a direct adaptation of the hit RPG', following Ashe's story in Ivalice.
Wikipedia: the Fox series "serves as a direct sequel to the original 1973 film and ignores the film's various sequels and prequels".
Wikipedia: the 1995 film "is a 1995 American science fiction martial arts film based on the Japanese manga of the same name by Buronson and Tetsuo Hara". Manga is the source.

Sibling adaptations of one source: the Disney+ drama is based on the web novel of the same title, and the manhwa row is that novel's webtoon (97 chapters, 'Original Story: Got W'). Neither is the other's source.

The 2005 Korean manhwa recounts the Grand Chase game's own prologue — Kaze'aze murdering the Kanavan Queen's retainer and steering her into the five-year war with Serdin — and MAL tracks it as a 30-volume, 150-chapter manhwa of the 2003 KOG MMO (AniList's own `source` field says ORIGINAL, so the claim rests on the shared story, hence medium confidence).
IGDB: an action game 'released as a tie-in for the 1999 Film', set immediately after Evie resurrects Imhotep.
The RTÉ/BBC series is based on Peter Foott's 2016 film, with the film's leads reprising Conor and Jock; this row is season 4.
Wikipedia: the RTÉ/BBC sitcom is "Based on the IFTA-winning 2016 film of the same name" by the same creator Peter Foott, following the film's characters; this row is season 3.
RTÉ/BBC's series is based on the 2016 film, with Peter Foott developing it and Alex Murphy/Chris Walley reprising Conor and Jock.
Wikipedia: the RTÉ/BBC sitcom is “based on the IFTA-winning 2016 film of the same name”, developed by Peter Foott with the film’s Conor and Jock; the series continues the film (this row is season 1).
Both adapt the light novel Mondaiji-tachi ga Isekai kara Kuru Sou Desu yo (AniList 75855): the anime and the manga each declare ADAPTATION to it; neither adapts the other.
Jikuu Bouken Nuumamonjaa is a comedy OVA produced for Chrono Trigger (it parodies the game's opening carnival with its own characters): same continuity, not a story adaptation.

Kodansha's manga adaptation of the French animated series (announced December 2020, serialised in Monthly Shōnen Sirius from the March 2021 issue) is the manga row; the paired row is Season 7 of the show.
AniList records the 2020 manga's source as VIDEO_GAME: the 38-chapter Ninjala serialisation adapts GungHo's 2020 Nintendo Switch game.
AniList records Ninjala the Animation (142274) with source VIDEO_GAME, and GungHo's 2020 Switch game is the franchise's game; the anime adapts it.

Wikipedia: Uwe Boll's film is based on the Alone in the Dark game series; the paired row is the 1992 original that created its protagonist Edward Carnby — a loose series-level adaptation, not a faithful adaptation of this title.
Wikipedia: the 1997 film's screenplay is based on the 1962-66 television series, with Ernest Borgnine reprising his role — the season 1 row is the show it adapts.
IGDB: "released prior to the film by the same name" and retells its story with a different ending sequence.
Wikipedia: "Cars 2 ... is a 2011 racing game based on the 2011 film of the same name."
The KBS2 series is "based on the webtoon of the same name" (Wikipedia); this row is that webtoon.

Wikipedia: the 2016 Rai series is "based on the eponymous 2013 film, also directed by Pif" (its own synopsis says "Inspired by Pierfrancesco “Pif” Diliberto's film"); this row is the series' first season.
Wikipedia: the RAI series is 'based on the eponymous 2013 film', also written and directed by Pif; show-level tie anchored on the season 2 row.

The seven-chapter manga states it is based on the PS3/360 game Sonic Generations; this 2024 row is that same game remastered (IGDB type Remaster, parentTitle 'Sonic Generations'), so the manga adapts the work this release presents — neither adapts the other.
The manga is 'Shirokishi Monogatari Episode 0: Dogma Senki', an original prequel manga to Level-5's game rather than an adaptation of its plot.
AniList records the anime's source as VISUAL_NOVEL and credits AQUAPLUS as original creator; it adapts this game's story (Mask of Truth / Futari no Hakuoro).
Two adaptations of Neil Simon's 1965 play: the 1968 film and the 1970–75 sitcom, which Wikipedia also derives from the play. Neither adapts the other.
Wikipedia: 'A live-action adaptation of the series aired from September 21 to November 2, 2022 on Wavve' — the 2022 series adapts this webtoon.
Hideaki Anno's 2004 film is 'adapted from the manga series Cutie Honey created by Go Nagai'.

Wikipedia: the Stan series is 'a spin-off continuation of the continuity established in the movies, and is the third installment in the Wolf Creek franchise', with John Jarratt's Mick Taylor and the first film's survivor Eve.
Both adapt Marvel's X-Men comics: the 2011 Madhouse Marvel Anime series and Bryan Singer's 2000 film; neither adapts the other.

Both adapt Yumi Hotta and Takeshi Obata's manga Hikaru no Go: AniList declares the 2001 anime an ADAPTATION of manga 30020 and TMDB tags the 2020 iQiyi drama 'based on manga'. Neither row adapts the other.

Both adapt the English fairy tale "Jack and the Beanstalk": the 2001 Henson/Hallmark miniseries is "based on the classic English tale" and the 2009 film is "from a story based on the classic fairy tale". Neither adapts the other.
Wikipedia: the 2023 SBS drama is based on the Kakao webtoon Gungminsahyeongtupyo (The Killing Vote), 12 episodes.

The 2010 film is built on the sketch show: "A 2010 film was made based on the characters in the show", and its plot follows Rafshan and Dzhumzhud from the series (show-wide tie, anchored on the season 2 row).
Wikipedia: the 2009 film 'is a live-action adaptation of the anime film of the same name created and produced by studio Production I.G' — a film-to-film tie, so related rather than adaptation.

Wikipedia: Dax Shepard's 2017 film is 'based on the 1977–1983 television series of the same name' created by Rick Rosner — a comedy remake of the show, so related, not an adaptation of any one season.
The July-December 2021 TV anime adapts the game — AniList records its source as VIDEO_GAME — released by Bandai Namco on 2021-06-24.
The 2022 Netflix film is "based on the webtoon Moral Sense by Gyeoul" (Wikipedia), which is this AniList row (its synonym list carries the film title).
Wikipedia: the Gantz films 'are based on Hiroya Oku's manga series, Gantz'; the 2010 film is the first of them.
Wikipedia: the CBS series "is a continuation of the 2011 film of the same name" and "takes place four years after the film's events" (Jake McDorman's Brian Finch inherits Eddie Morra's NZT story).
The 2023 TVING series is based on the webtoon of the same name by Lee Won-sik and Ggulchan.

Mann's 2006 film is 'an adaptation of the 1980s television series of the same name' he produced: Crockett and Tubbs re-cast in a rebooted continuity with a new story, so it is a feature reworking of the show, not an adaptation of one season.
The single-episode ONA (2014-08-08) adapts the game — AniList records its source as VIDEO_GAME — released by Koei Tecmo on 2014-08-28.

Wikipedia on the 2003 Tartakovsky micro-series: "Its success led to it being spun off as the CGI series The Clone Wars in 2008" — this row is that series' third and final season (Volume Two), and the 2008 theatrical film launched the CGI series, so the film spins off the 2003 show rather than adapting it.
Yuichi Fukuda's 2026 film is an adaptation of Yuto Suzuki's manga; TMDB tags the film 'based on manga' and its synopsis is the manga's premise (retired hitman Sakamoto).
The Japanese live-action series (2005-2007) adapts Yoko Kamio's manga; this row is its 2007 second season.
Wikipedia: the 2005 TBS drama 'is based on the manga series Boys Over Flowers by Yoko Kamio' — the 244-chapter manga row is its source (the 2007 sequel season continues the same adaptation).
Wikipedia: the 2009 KBS2 series is 'based on the Japanese manga series Boys Over Flowers ... written and illustrated by Yoko Kamio'; TMDB keyword 'based on manga'.

Wikipedia: the 2015 SBS drama was 'adapted from the KTOON webtoon of the same title by Seo Soo-kyung a/k/a Man Chwi' — the AniList row credits Manchi and carries the same 냄새를 보는 소녀 title. This row is the show's only season.

Both adapt one source (Jules Verne's 1875 Mysterious Island: the 2005 Hallmark miniseries is 'very loosely based on' it and Cy Endfield's 1961 film is another adaptation of the same novel — siblings, neither is the other's source.)
AniList: "An adaptation of the SILENT HILL f video game with a new ending written by the original scenario writer, Ryukishi07" (Young Ace UP, 2026).
Takashi Miike's 2017 film is based on Hiroaki Samura's Blade of the Immortal manga.

Both adapt Goethe’s Faust and neither adapts the other: AniList describes the 2008 one-volume manga as the “manga version of the play Faust by Johann Wolfgang von Goethe” (Goethe is credited as original story), and Švankmajer’s 1994 film is a free adaptation of Marlowe’s Doctor Faustus and Goethe’s Faust.
Wikipedia: the 2007 film "is a film version of the TV series Cidade dos Homens", with the same creators (Meirelles/Morelli) and characters; this row is season 2 of that series.
The 2007 film is loosely based on the 1960s animated series; the tie is to the show as a whole, anchored on the season 1 row.

Both adapt Marvel's Fantastic Four comics: the 2015 film is "based on the Marvel Comics superhero team" and the 1994 animated series draws on the same comics; neither adapts the other (cf. batch-047 #4675).
The 2008 film continues the HBO series (same writer-director Michael Patrick King and cast, set four years after the finale); this row is season 2 of that series.
The 1979 film is the show’s pilot, shot as the pilot and released theatrically instead of airing (Glen A. Larson, same cast); the row is season 1.
IGDB: the PlayStation game is the tie-in with the 1997 film, using its Mr. Freeze / Poison Ivy / Bane plot and its Batgirl.
The 2003 game is the licensed tie-in of MTV's claymation show; season 4 (2001) was the latest season aired at its release.
The Fox series is 'based on the Lethal Weapon film franchise created by Shane Black' and reboots it; the 1987 film is the franchise's first entry, and this is its season 1 row.
Keith Gordon's 2003 film is based on Dennis Potter's 1986 BBC serial of the same name.
Wikipedia's One Missed Call index lists the Dark Horse manga as 'a manga based on the Japanese film'; the manga synopsis matches the 2003 film (future voicemails, candy in the mouths).
The 2006 Nippon TV series is the live-action adaptation of the manga, as its TMDB overview states ("TV Live-action adaptation of the manga of the same name").

Wikipedia: the Kids' WB cartoon "features characters from the science fiction film Men in Black" — it continues the film's agency and agents as its own series, so it spins off the film rather than adapting it.

Wikipedia: the Kids' WB cartoon "features characters from the science fiction film Men in Black" and continues its agency and agents as its own series — a spin-off, not an adaptation. This is the season-3 row; seasons 1 (batch-047) and 2 (batch-081) already carry the same edge.

Wikipedia: the Kids’ WB cartoon “features characters from the science fiction film Men in Black” and continues the agency as its own series; the season-1 row carries the same edge (batch-047 #4627) and this row is season 2.
Wikipedia: "The show features characters from the science fiction film Men in Black"; this row is Season 4 of that animated series.
Wikipedia: Angry Birds Toons 'is based on Rovio Entertainment's Angry Birds franchise', and this game is the franchise's 2009 origin; the series' episodes dramatise its birds-versus-pigs premise.
Fuji TV's 1991 eleven-episode drama adapts Fumi Saimon's manga Tokyo Love Story.
David Production's 2013 anime adapts Compile Heart/Idea Factory's 2010 game — AniList records its source as VIDEO_GAME.
Shiro Amano's Chain of Memories manga adapts the 2004 Game Boy Advance game (AniList source: video game).

Wikipedia: the Paramount+ series "is the prequel to the 2000 film Sexy Beast", following Gal Dove, Don Logan and Teddy Bass as younger men in 1990s London; it spins off the film's characters rather than adapting it.
Both adapt Marvel’s X-Men comics — the 1992 animated series and Bryan Singer’s 2000 film “based on the superhero team from Marvel Comics” — neither adapts the other.
A live-action film adaptation of Hatsuharu's manga premiered in March 2025 (Wikipedia), matching this film row's 2025-03-14 release.

Wikipedia: the 1999 film is "Adapting the 1960s television series The Wild Wild West by Michael Garrison", with Will Smith and Kevin Kline as Jim West and Artemus Gordon; the film adapts the show as a whole, carried by its season 1 row.
Ryuhei Kitamura's 2003 live-action film is an adaptation of Yu Koyama's manga Azumi (1994-2008, 48 volumes).
The 2010 film is an adaptation of the 2003 Ubisoft game of the same name (with elements of its sequels), scripted from a story by series creator Jordan Mechner.
Konami's 1989 NES game is 'one of the first video games based on the 1987 Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles animated series'; this row is the cartoon's eighth season.

Konami's 1989 four-player arcade game is named alongside the NES game in Wikipedia's statement that both were 'one of the first video games based on the 1987 ... animated series'; this row is the cartoon's eighth season.

edits.to: One-volume manga adaptation of the 1984 American television series Airwolf, by Minoru Nonaka.

Jiro Kuwata's Batman manga, serialised in Shonen King from April 1966 to May 1967 during the Batman craze that followed the 1966 television series, is an adaptation of the American Batman comics rather than of the show. Chip Kidd collected the surviving chapters in English in 2008 as Bat-Manga!: The Secret History of Batman in Japan.

The United Kingdom of Euchronia is thrown into chaos following the assassination of its king... Our Hero, the Traveler Will, and his Fairy Companion Gallica, race to Grand Trad to undertake a Special Mission. Discover the bonds that form between eight races across three countries.

(Source: Manga Plus)
Short animation by Komazaki Tomomi.

Sengoku Rance is the tenth release of the Rance series launched by Alicesoft. The story takes place during the 4th sengoku (warring states) era of JAPAN, an area of the Rance World which parodies medieval real-world Japan.

Sengoku Rance picks up where Rance 6 left off. Rance, after saving the nation of Zeth from destruction, ran away so he won't have to marry the princess. He and Sill ended up in JAPAN for a hotspring trip, upsetting the power balance of JAPAN, and sets the unification of its provinces in motion. Meanwhile, an ancient evil power stirs from its slumber...

The actual story of this manga follows the daughter of one of the feudal lord defeated by Rance. She is the last guardian of the three sacred treasure rumored to end the conflict in JAPAN and is now protected by Uesugi Kenshin.
Based on the manga by U-Jin.

edits.from:
A talent bestowed upon a monster. Is it a blessing—or a curse? K, a legendary boxing trainer who has produced numerous world champions, is searching for his “final disciple.” Then he encounters Yu, a boy in a back alley who simply stands there, taking punch after punch. The boy shows neither anger nor fighting spirit, yet K sees in him something beyond genius: a talent of unfathomable potential.

Under K’s guidance, Yu steps into the boxing ring. With an overwhelming strength that can only be described as monstrous, he begins his ascent toward the pinnacle of the boxing world. Standing in his way are champions who stake their pride on skills honed to perfection, and fighters who have overcome the limits of talent through sheer effort. Each carries a dream they refuse to surrender and a reason to keep fighting. Their clashes with the monster shake even the foundations of the lives they have built.

And what does Yu himself seek at the end of his fists? The life of one “monster” intertwines with the lives of those who fight him. Beyond talent and hard work, glory and defeat, a story begins—one that asks what it truly means to be strong.

(Source: Crunchyroll)

(Source: Crunchyroll)
Five-volume manga adaptation of Takashi Miike's 2004 film Zebraman by Reiji Yamada, which told its own story around the hero's relationship with his two children.

While it initially started as a 4-koma gag manga based on the popular battle royale game "Fortnite", the manga has since been releasing as 10-page weekly magazine. The comic has spun into a story about Roy Bic's quest to win the Fortnite World Cup. Along with his dog, Coro, and a few of his friends he tries to reach the top of the world!

edits.from: Lead by fate, the two siblings, Senel and Shirley, arrived on the "Legacy", a Relic Ship made by the ancient people of the past. There, they both meet with a band of unlikely allies, learning about the state of the world and discover the path they each must take. This is a tale of destiny about their meeting and the bonds forged between them

Takumi Harada moves with his family to a mountain town in Okayama and loses faith in his pitching, until his classmate Gō Nagakura insists on forming a battery with him.
ended

Life is like a game of baduk: you move your pieces, claim your territory, and use every strategy you can to win. When Jang Geu-Rae fails to go pro in baduk, he leaves the game behind for the corporate world... only to find that it's much the same. Starting a new job with just a GED and a recommendation, Geu-Rae has new pieces and a new board to explore--can baduk help him survive the corporate battleground?(Source: Tapas)
ended

After years of being bullied, Choi Baekho snaps one day and finds himself standing over his pummeled tormentors with bloody fists and gaps in his memory. Now, as Shinheung High's "crazy dog," he's gnashing his teeth at all those who rely on the strength of numbers. But when his efforts to beat 11th grade's top gun Do Changsoo get him mixed up with the mob, Baekho must join forces with his own rival. Can this unlikely ally help Baekho control his "switch" and become every bully's worst nightmare?

(Source: Tapas)

to: A Secret and a Fruitless Flower

edits.to:
Saebom, a Sergeant of the Special Forces, and Ihyeon, a Detective Sergeant of Saeyang Police Station, are high school friends who enter into a marriage of convenience so that they can qualify to buy an apartment together, while a mysterious and seemingly contagious virus tear through their city of Saeyang. Saebom and Ihyeon move into their dream home only to find that the new virus that turns people violent and thirsty for blood has come knocking at their door.

(Source: WEBTOONS)
Capcom's 1989 arcade platform game based on the 1988 film of the same name; one of two Willow games Capcom published that year, the other for the NES.
Manga version of Jeanne Darc's story.
ended

A manga adaptation of the beloved X-Men: The Animated Series.

In X-Men, Vol. 1, Jubilation Lee is a teenager with a secret: she's a mutant, the next level of human evolution, and has fantastic powers. All she wants is a normal life with trips to the mall to get away from her parents, but when the mutant-hunting robots known as Sentinels come after her, that normal life is pushed out of her reach! Discover the X-Men—mutant heroes hated and feared by a world they're sworn to protect—alongside Jubilee in this classic manga series.

Ragnarok, the End of the World, draws near. Odin, Lord of the Gods, summons Lenneth Valkyrie, one of the three Goddesses of Destiny. Lenneth is assigned the task of recruiting men's souls worthy of becoming Einherjar - heroes that will serve the Gods during Ragnarok. As Lenneth travels Midgard, the plane of mortals, collecting souls, she is faced with events that cause her to question who and what she is.
Single-volume manga adaptation of the 2007 role-playing game Eternal Sonata, drawn by Mimei Kuroi and published by ASCII Media Works.

Kaze'aze managed to infiltrate the Kanavan  Kingdom by murdering the Kanavan Queen's most loyal and trusted retainer, and then disguising herself as him. As a result, Kaze'aze was able to get close to the Queen and entice her with the ways of darkness. Kaze'aze blinded the Queen of Kanavan's eyes to truth and led her to wage a five-year war against the Serdin Kingdom. All of Bermesiah  Continent was devastated; many heroes fell in battle, and even the Queen of Serdin sacrificed her life in hopes of ending the fighting.
The death of the Queen of Serdin broke Kaze'aze's hold over the Queen of Kanavan, who, after finally regaining her senses, erupted with fury over Kaze'aze's treachery. Kaze'aze escaped before the Queen of Kanavan could execute her. This lead the Queen to dispatch Trackers to punish the Queen of Darkness. But after years of searching, she was nowhere to be found and the Queen's Trackers vanished as well; forcing the Queen of Kanavan to abandon her search.
The Serdin Kingdom experienced a series of bizarre incidents related to Kaze'aze after the Five-Year War: these events revealed that Kaze'aze manipulated the Kanavan and Serdin Kingdoms into fighting each other. The
ended

Computer programmer Angela Bennett discovers a shadowy group of cyber terrorists who completely erase her true identity. Falsely labeled a criminal, she finds herself on the run, and she'll never stop until she's got her life back.

Ju-On - video side - is the manga adaptation of the Japanese horror movie that spawned an enormous franchise in Japan... and inspired a blockbuster Hollywood remake! This chilling tale of murder, secrets and revenge centers on a home and the ugly events that transpired there. The place now has new owners, but there is a vile presence that permeates the building and pollutes every surface. What wickedness set off this unstoppable angry spirit? Why has its bloody grudge infected the home and its inhabitants? In the spirit of The Ring, Ju-On delivers a dark warning of a cursed spirit and the corrupting influence it has on the living.

Manga about a hedgehog boy named Nicky Parlouzer who can turn into Sonic the Hedgehog. Along with Miles "Tails" Prower, Sonic fights Dr. Eggman. Nicky has several friends in the "real world", including little John, his girlfriend Amy (a prototype/first incarnation of Amy Rose), and Charmy (a prototype/first incarnation of Charmy Bee). (Source: AniList)
During the period of the ‘Provinces at war’, many lives were lost. A castle architect discovers the possible role of a tea room as a place for warriors to regain humanity.

These cute, cartoony characters hate their lives and just want to escape! An official adaptation of The Amazing Digital Circus animated series.

Are you ready to witness the most jaw-dropping, heart-stopping, mind-bending paraphernalia you've ever laid your eyes upon? Then allow your ringmaster, Caine, to welcome you to the Amazing Digital Circus!

After putting on a strange headset she discovers in an abandoned building, a young woman finds herself inside the Amazing Digital Circus! Transformed into a cartoon jester named Pomni, she discovers she's trapped in this glitchy digital world alongside a whole host of colorful characters. Will she be able to find the exit door and escape, or will she be stuck here until she loses her mind?

(Source: VIZ Media)

In 2150 A.D. space pilot Takeru and human computer Martha come across a giant ship containing two mechanical beings, Sara and Ru Mi, who warn that the alien Gump is heading for Earth. With forty minutes left before the invasion, Takeru takes the Solvalou to strike the Gump base on planet Andoa. A CGI film adaptation of Namco's 1982 arcade game Xevious.

"Tougenrou" is a red light district where notable people gather. All sorts of foolishness unfolds there every night.

What is the sad fate awaiting the mysterious beauty named Urara and the prostitute named Byakuran?

Masaki's older brother's recommendation landed him a part-time job at a theme park, where a person in a bear costume greets him by name; as Masaki falls for Oosawa, a 14-year age gap and old scars complicate things.
Takumi Harada, already the best pitcher in his region, is pursued by catcher Gō Nagakura, who wants to form a battery with him.

195 page Manga/Strategy Guide, released only in Japan from Wanpakku Comics.
Ten-volume comic adaptation of Kwak Jae-yong's 2001 film My Sassy Girl, following Geon-woo and the girl he meets on the subway.

May 1, 1945. Berlin. As the Red Army raises the Soviet flag, a group of Nazi officers conduct a ritual using the slaughter in the city to bring back the LDO, supermen whose coming would bring the world's destruction. Their success remains unknown.

Present day. Suwahara City. Ren Fujii spends his days at the hospital due to a violent fight with his best friend, Shirou. He tries to value what he has left to him, but he is haunted by Shirou's words: "Everyone who remains in this city eventually loses their minds." and a recurring dream of a guillotine, murderers, and the black clad knights pursuing them.

(Source: Anime News Network, edited)

Includes episode 0.
Two-volume manga adaptation of Vanillaware's 2013 game Dragon's Crown, following six adventurers questing for the titular relic in the kingdom of Hydeland.
Yumiko Igarashi's one-volume manga adaptation of L. Frank Baum's The Wonderful Wizard of Oz.

In this world and the next, both good and evil exist. But who do you call when evil spirits from the afterlife escape to prey on innocent human lives? You call the Counters, people with supernatural abilities, who also happen to run a noodle shop. When one's killed, an ordinary high school student is unexpectedly chosen to take their place. The seemingly mundane life of So Mun takes a drastic turn as his body changes (curly hair now included) and he starts to show a talent for his new role. (Source: Tapas)

The story revolves around Koume who enters a private high school. She hears from her friend Sasuga that if she enters the tea ceremony club, she can eat snacks. They bring along their classmates Mikaeru and Momiji to join the club with her. The president of the club is 11th grade Ayame.
Pacto de Sangre (Blood Pact) is a Spanish-language crime drama thriller about four lifelong friends whose lives spiral out of control after an accidental death at a bachelor party.

A TV special animation of the Romance of the Three Kingdoms. In the late Eastern Han, with the imperial court powerless and the Yellow Turban rebels ravaging the country, Liu Bei - a descendant of the Han house - rises with his sworn brothers Guan Yu and Zhang Fei, and by strategy and strange measures cuts down the rebel armies one after another.
An Isuzu truck company commissioned short from Tekken about a freight truck driver who takes pride in his work.

A story-driven experience about two doctors traversing backwards through a dying man’s memories to artificially fulfill his last wish.
(Source: Steam)
Pacto de Sangre (Blood Pact) is a Spanish-language crime drama thriller about four lifelong friends whose lives spiral out of control after an accidental death at a bachelor party.

Based on the action RPG of the same name.

The story follows a man's journey seeking revenge on a dragon who stole his heart. On his way, the man is brought back to life as an ‘Arisen’. An action adventure about a man challenged by demons who represent the seven deadly sins of humans.

(Source: Netflix)
Three-volume manga adaptation of the 1999 PlayStation game Koudelka, following the amnesiac Koudelka through the haunted Nemeton monastery in 1898 Wales.

After the death of his estranged father, a young man travels to a strange countryside town to take care of the funeral arrangements. With his own life in shambles, he decides to stay but finds the village people less than welcoming. Their odd behavior and the things his father left behind, leads him on a dangerous path to a truth that might be better left buried.

(Source: Spottoon)

Dani Kang sometimes wonders what her life would have been like if she had run away on her wedding day. She was a successful career woman before getting married, but now she is divorced, unemployed, and a single mother of one. During her divorce, her life got turned upside down as she found herself not only struggling to re-enter the professional world after having taken a long break from it but in desperate need of a home as well. When her dear friend, Eunho Cha, who is a successful author and a chief editor at a publishing company, asks Dani to help him find a housekeeper, she decides to take up that job herself without his knowledge. Eventually, she gets discovered and receives help from Eunho, but then their lives become even more intertwined when Dani applies for an open position at his company. Will they be able to navigate through all the personal and professional challenges lying ahead of them?

 (Source: Tappytoon)
Graduation Work of Shin Hosokawa at Tama Art University.

A short fable about people who try to achieve the impossible. Wing, who has been shut up in a room for ages, dreams of freedom as he watches an angel doll hanging from the windowsill. He makes several attempts to become an angel himself.

edits.from: Batman Beyond: Return of the Joker (also known as Batman of the Future: Return of the Joker in Europe and Australia) is a 2000 American direct-to-video animated film featuring the comic book superhero Batman and his archenemy, the Joker. It is set in the continuity of the animated series Batman Beyond, in which Bruce Wayne has retired from crime fighting, giving the mantle of Batman to high school student Terry McGinnis, and serves as a sequel to both Batman: The Animated Series and The New Batman Adventures. As in the TV series, Will Friedle and Kevin Conroy star as Terry McGinnis and Bruce Wayne, respectively. Mark Hamill, who played the Joker opposite Conroy in Batman: The Animated Series and The New Batman Adventures, reprises his role.
edits.to: A scrolling beat 'em up developed by Kemco for the Game Boy Color, PlayStation and Nintendo 64, based on the 2000 animated film. Players control Terry McGinnis, the new Batman, fighting the Jokerz gang across Gotham City to stop the revived Joker.
Eri Okazaki's graduation work from 2016 at Tama Art University.

A manga anthology, based on the first Valkyrie Profile Game "Lenneth". It's a collection of several comedy short stories by 10 different mangakas.

Note: Released in Enix Supercomic Gekijoh Volume 22, 24, 26, 29, 34, 38, 46 and 50.

Loosely based on L.F. Baum's novel, The Wizard of Oz. Original manga done by Itsuki Natsumi.

A nuclear war has killed most of humanity and split the USA into six warring states. By 2021, a legend has grown up about the fabled city of OZ where everything still works. Scientist Felicia sets out in search of it with the mercenary Muto and android 1019. At the end of the quest they only discover a military base and a madman.

A mercenary was hired by a girl to bring her to the mythical Oz (a paradise) where her missing brother supposedly lived. Accompanying them was a cyborg sent by her brother. But Oz was not the paradise it seemed and her brother was not as sane as he was smart.

(Source: AniDB)
Webtoon adaptation of the 2023 JTBC drama King the Land, following hotel heir Gu Won and Cheon Sa-rang.
Graduation work of Chihiro Hirosawa at Tama Art University.
One-volume manga adaptation of the 1995 film Waterworld, set on a flooded Earth where the Mariner searches for the last dry land.

edits.from:
After his business goes bankrupt, 30 something Kyung-Min (Oh Jung-Se) kills his wife impulsively. Hiding his anger, he seeks out his former middle school classmate Jong-Suk (Yang Ik-June). Jong-Suk now works as a ghostwriter for an autobiography, but he dreams of writing his own novel. For the first time in 15 years they meet. Kyung-Min and Jong-Suk both hide their own current situations and begin to talk about their middle school days.

At their middle school, they were classified by their wealth and grades. Kyung-Min and Jong-Suk were at the bottom. They were called pigs. They were bullied by a ruling class called dogs. When they were called pigs they got angry, but couldn't do anything against the dogs. Then a king of pigs appears - Chul (Kim Hye-Na). Kyung-Min and Jong-Suk became to rely on Chul-Yi.

Now, leading Jong-Suk to their middle school grounds, Kyung-Min discloses the shocking truth to Jong-Suk of what happened 15 years ago.

(Source: Asian Media Wiki)
edits.to: After his business goes bankrupt, thirty-something Kyung-Min kills his wife impulsively. Hiding his anger, he seeks out his former middle-school classmate Jong-Suk, now a ghostwriter who dreams of writing his own novel. Over their first meeting in fifteen years both hide their present situations and talk about school, where they were classed as pigs by the ruling dogs - until a king of pigs, Chul, appeared and they came to rely on her. Leading Jong-Suk back to the school grounds, Kyung-Min discloses the shocking truth of what happened fifteen years ago.
One-volume manga based on the 2005 Tecmo game Fatal Frame III: The Tormented, following Miku Hinasaki into the haunted mansion.

An experiment concerning the attempts at creating a 'moving image' long before the invention of cinema. A re-experiencing of the history of 'magic with light' unfolds through devices and techniques including flip-book animation and Muybridge's photographs in motion zoopraxiscope.

A man wakes up, tied to a crucifix. He is a district attorney, held prisoner by a serial killer named Tang Lee. As the story unfolds, we follow Tang Lee’s descent from average nobody to murderer, his victims all criminals who had escaped justice. (Source: WEBTOON)

Note: Includes three extra chapters.

Tamura Kouji, Naoya's former co-worker from Yasashii Kankei, finally returns to Okayama to take over his father's car business. Though he still has Naoya on his mind, his family and friends give him a warm welcome and invite him to a class reunion. There, he meets a man that looks strangely like the one who robbed him of his first love, and is just as disagreeable. But while bringing him home in a drunken stupor, Tamura realizes there may just be more to the man than he thinks.

Based on the world-famous novels by Anne and Serge Golon (a husband and wife team--she did the writing, he the research). The beautiful Angelique is force-married to the noble Joffrey de Peyrac, although she is in love with another noble, Phillipe. However, she gradually falls in love with Joffrey but right then he's accused to be a sorcerer.

(Source: PRISMS)
Comedy manga by Sankichi Hinodeya following Goggles and Team Blue through Inkopolis's Turf Wars, launched as a one-shot in 2015 and serialised in CoroCoro Comic.

edits.from: Officer Choi Mu-gak lost his younger sister to a barcode-murder case and lost his ability to taste, smell, and feel pain. He then meets a girl named Oh Cho-rim, who is the only witness to the murder case and possesses a special sixth sense, which is the ability to see smells.
edits.to:
After Sae-ah loses her parents to arson, the accident leaves her with the ability to see smells. Another fire puts her in the path of police officer Pyeongan Kim. Though he doesn’t believe in her ability at first, the two team up to solve cases, and he quickly realizes the power Sae-ah holds. Although her ability helps her solve all kinds of crimes, she’s yet to solve the biggest mystery of them all: who killed her parents?

(Source: WEBTOONS)

Note: The physical volumes only compile the first 62 chapters, five parts
Manga version of the play Faust by Johann Wolfgang von Goethe.

lowConfidence.reason: Wikipedia: the 2019 game is "based on the film series of the same name" and set two years after The Blair Witch Project; it shares the franchise/continuity of the 2016 film rather than adapting it.

Franchise neighbours only: this 2012 manga credits Ring author Koji Suzuki as its story writer, and the 2019 film is Hideo Nakata's Ring installment loosely based on Suzuki's novel Tide — but no source ties the manga to that film, which sits in its own continuity.

Same franchise (Saban's Power Rangers) but not the same continuity: the 2017 film is a reboot loosely adapting Mighty Morphin's 1993 pilot, while this row is the 2016 TV-continuity season (Dino Super Charge); no source ties the two productions.
Same franchise but separate continuity: the 2017 film reboots the property from Mighty Morphin's pilot, while this row is the 2018 TV season (Super Ninja Steel); no source ties the two productions.

Franchise tie only: the 2008 film is a standalone sequel to Uwe Boll's 2005 film, itself loosely based on the Alone in the Dark games, and this is the second game — no source says the film adapts the 1993 game.

Same franchise but not the same continuity: the 2017 film is a reboot that "loosely adapts 'Day of the Dumpster'", the Mighty Morphin pilot, while this row is the 2015 TV-continuity season (Dino Charge); no source ties the two productions.
Same franchise but not the same continuity: the 2017 film is a reboot of the Mighty Morphin story while this row is the 2019 TV-continuity season (Beast Morphers); no source ties the two productions.

Weakest whole-tale tie: Mizuno's Princess Mermaid is the third of her fractured fairy-tale retellings (published in French as La Petite Sirène) and Disney's series follows the 1989 film, itself based on Andersen's 1837 tale; neither adapts the other. Held at low because no source I read states Mizuno's link outright.

Same franchise (Saban’s Power Rangers) but not the same continuity: Wikipedia calls the 2017 film “a reboot that loosely adapts ‘Day of the Dumpster’”, while this row is the 2012 season (Samurai/Super Samurai).
Same franchise, separate continuity: the 2017 film is “a reboot that loosely adapts ‘Day of the Dumpster’” (Mighty Morphin’s pilot), while this row is the 2022 season (Dino Fury).

Same franchise, separate continuity: the 2017 film is 'a reboot that loosely adapts "Day of the Dumpster"' while this row is the 2008 Jungle Fury season (adapted from Sentai's Gekiranger); no source ties the two productions.

Circumstantial: the 1975 NBC series about Daniel Westin is listed among the television adaptations of Wells's The Invisible Man, which the 2020 film is "loosely based on"; no source ties the two productions, so low confidence.
Circumstantial: the 1975 NBC series (an original protagonist, Daniel Westin) and Whale's 1933 film both draw on Wells's The Invisible Man; no source ties the two productions, so low confidence.

Both claim Homer's Odyssey as source — the 1997 Hallmark miniseries and TMDB 1698863, an unaffiliated 2026 film whose synopsis says 'based on the Ancient Greek epic' and which TMDB tags as a mockbuster; no production tie is documented.

Circumstantial: Disney+'s 2025 Mexican series is a sequel to 2023's 'Viaje al centro de la Tierra' set in a 'Verne Dimension' with Admiral Nemo and the Calliope (Verne's improved Nautilus), so it shares Verne's fictional universe with the 1916 film but adapts no Verne plot. Held back for review.

Circumstantial: the 2025 Disney+ series is a kids' adventure in a 'Verne Dimension' (Admiral Nemo, the Calliope) and a sequel to 'Viaje al centro de la Tierra', not an adaptation of the novel; only the Verne universe is shared with Disney's 1954 film. Held back for review.
Both are Kowaremono hentai works (the 2014 manga is the source of a 2015 OVA of that name), but no source ties the 2000 OVA Slave Doll to the manga — same franchise name only.
Loose Mexican reworking of Verne's premise (same title, a journey to the centre of the Earth); no source states an adaptation, unlike the 1959 film, which is one.

duplicates.note: TMDB's 5-episode 2018 "series" is the first season of Telltale's Minecraft: Story Mode re-issued as an interactive Netflix title ("the first season, excluding the DLC episodes, was released on Netflix in late 2018"), not a separate adaptation. Keep the game row (IGDB is native for games, 5 episodes of season 1).

One work twice: TMDB files the Spanish-Japanese co-production as a 26-episode 1983 series while AniList files the same 26-episode Nippon Animation production under its 1987 Japanese broadcast title (アニメ80日間世界一周). Keep the AniList anime row (native provider for the anime kind, episode count matches).
TMDB files one ten-part Showtime documentary both as a 10-episode series (correct shape) and as a 585-minute film; IMDb tt1494191 is on both rows.
The 1985 row is the six-part miniseries cut of the same production (same director, same 6 parts); the theatrical film row is the canonical work.

Keep the AniList row (native provider for anime, 50 episodes matching AniList) and drop TMDB's season-1 row, which packs the whole of Battle Planet (52 episodes counting the two specials) into one season; this is the same show, not two adaptations.
